name: Self-Driving Car
summary: An autonomous vehicle system that continuously perceives, plans, and executes driving behavior in real-world environments to achieve navigation goals.

primary_interpretation.driver: Persistent real-time agency combined with direct control over high-consequence physical systems
primary_interpretation.constraint: Goals remain externally defined and bounded, with strong safety constraints and oversight

agii.evidence: Self-driving systems continuously perceive surroundings, plan trajectories, and execute driving actions over extended periods without continuous human input.
agii.interpretation: This is sustained, real-time agency with ongoing task continuation and adaptation in an open environment.
agii.implication: AGII is high due to continuous, self-sustained task execution under dynamic conditions.

casx.evidence: The system directly controls a vehicle in real-world environments, affecting safety, mobility, and potentially life-critical outcomes.
casx.interpretation: Its real-world impact is substantial due to physical actuation, environmental interaction, and high stakes.
casx.implication: CASX is high because the system can produce significant real-world effects.

trajectory.evidence: Autonomous driving systems are improving rapidly in perception, planning, and deployment scale.
trajectory.interpretation: The field is evolving quickly toward broader capability and deployment.

change_levers.increase_risk: Broader deployment in complex environments, reduced human oversight, and integration with wider transportation systems
change_levers.decrease_risk: Strict safety constraints, limited operational domains, and strong monitoring and fallback mechanisms

classification_notes.inevitable_under_normal_use: Conditional — autonomous operation is normal, but risk depends on environment and safeguards

main_uncertainty: Extent to which future systems increase autonomy beyond bounded navigation tasks
